reasons: The original Slurm job requested memory per CPU (`--mem-per-cpu=4096`), but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems where memory is scheduled/enforced this may under-allocate memory and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job used a job array (`--array=2500-2508`), but the Flux resource section does not express any array/iteration mechanism; this changes the effective workload size and throughput characteristics.

The original Slurm job constrained placement to a specific partition (`--partition=bigmem`) and disabled hyperthreading (`--hint=nomultithread`), but the Flux resource section has no corresponding constraints; this can materially change the allocated hardware and performance.
issues: Because the array mechanism is omitted, the MATLAB invocation no longer receives the per-task indices (`$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID`, `$SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID`), so it will not run the intended parameter sweep.
